author: Brenn Allen Flores
title: A woman took her unusually violent horse to an animal communicator, and what it was trying to say apparently saved her life - NewsBreak
text:
By Brenn Allen Flores ,
6 hours ago Image by mindfrieze, CC BY-SA 2.0. A horse’s strange behavior led one Florida equestrian content creator to seek medical care, eventually resulting in the discovery of a Chiari malformation that required brain surgery . Taylor, who posts about her horses under the TikTok account @foxhallfarm, recently shared the story of how her horse Nemo’s behavior changed after the pair moved to a new farm
As detailed by BroBible , she said Nemo appeared normal when he was outside but became aggressive when she brought him into the barn. “He was fine outside, but the second I brought him in the barn, he became very violent, and it was really out of character,” Taylor said in a video about the experience. “So I called the animal communicator.”
Taylor said she contacted an animal communicator after struggling to explain the horse’s sudden change. During the session, she was told that Nemo was repeatedly communicating about a problem involving the brain and pressure in the head.
The Horse Was Warning Taylor About Her Brain “Brain, brain do this to me. Brain underwater, brain squish, brain pressure,” revealed Taylor. Taylor initially believed the comments were about Nemo because she had previously worked as a veterinary technician and said she thought the horse could have a brain tumor. However, the conversation changed when the communicator told her the messages were about Taylor rather than the horse.
She then decided to speak with her doctor, eventually undergoing an MRI that revealed a Chiari malformation. Chiari malformation is a structural condition in which part of the cerebellum extends into the spinal canal. Mayo Clinic says it can happen when the skull is shaped differently or is smaller than usual, leaving less room for the brain and pushing tissue downward. Type 1 is the most common form and can first cause symptoms during late childhood or adulthood.
https://www.tiktok.com/@foxhallfarm/photo/7688141678661750047?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc The condition does not always require treatment. Many people with Chiari malformation have no symptoms, but others can develop headaches, neck pain, balance problems, numbness, dizziness and problems with swallowing. Mayo Clinic notes that an MRI is commonly used to diagnose the condition and look at the brain and upper spinal cord.
Taylor said she eventually underwent surgery after her MRI showed the condition. She later documented her recovery online and said she was able to return to riding Nemo less than three weeks after the operation, following the removal of her surgical sutures.
“In less than three weeks I am back to riding him and I no longer feel at war with my body,” Taylor said in an update shared with her followers. Her account does not establish that Nemo actually diagnosed her condition, but rather that his unusual behavior prompted her to seek the medical evaluation that led to the diagnosis.
Research does show that horses respond to changes in their environment and can display measurable behavioral and physiological responses to stressful situations. A study published in Frontiers in Psychology found that horses showed changes in heart rate and behavior when exposed to different situations, although those responses varied between individual animals and settings.
Research involving horses and humans has also examined stress responses during equine-assisted activities. A 2023 review in Frontiers in Veterinary Science looked at physiological stress markers during interactions between people and horses, although the authors noted that results across the field are mixed and that more controlled research is needed.
Taylor has continued to share her recovery and life with Nemo on social media. Her account of the experience has connected the horse’s unusual behavior with a medical problem that she said she had not previously understood, while the medical side of the story remains grounded in the MRI findings and treatment she received.
